title: Bousfield–Smith bounded-subobject lemma for local equivalences
statement: Fix a universe of small sets and $\mathrm{sS}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{sSet})$ with the Reedy model structure and simplicial mapping sets of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. Fix a monomorphism $f:P\hookrightarrow Q$. An $f$-local object is a Reedy fibrant $Z$ for which $\operatorname{Map}(Q,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(P,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. An $f$-local equivalence $u:X\to Y$ is a map inducing a weak homotopy equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(X,Z)$ for every $f$-local $Z$. For a simplicial space put $|X|=|\coprod_{p,q\geq0}X_{p,q}|$. There is an uncountable regular small cardinal $\gamma$, depending only on $f$, with the following property: for every monomorphism $X\hookrightarrow Y$ that is an $f$-local equivalence and every simplicial subspace $C\subseteq Y$ with $|C|<\gamma$, there is a simplicial subspace $D\subseteq Y$ such that $C\subseteq D$, $|D|<\gamma$, and the inclusion $X\cap D\hookrightarrow D$ is an $f$-local equivalence. Intersections and subspaces are taken in every bidegree. Regular means that a union of fewer than $\gamma$ sets of size less than $\gamma$ has size less than $\gamma$. No localized model structure is assumed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\mathrm{sS}^{[1]}$. By currying, this is a category of Set-valued presheaves on the small category $(\Delta\times\Delta)\times[1]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Sets have pullbacks, given by pairs with equal images. The Set and presheaf clauses of [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] therefore make $\mathcal A$ locally presentable. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-local-equivalences-accessible] to $f$ and denote its replete subcategory by $\mathcal B=W_f^{\mathrm{mono}}$. Fix the regular cardinal $\lambda$ and small generating family supplied there. In particular $\mathcal B$ is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$. This supplies both hypotheses of condition (i) of the accessible-subdiagram criterion, without assuming a localized model structure.

source.place: Lemmas 4.5–4.6, printed p. 43; monomorphism-restricted accessibility is the separately stated auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-functor-presentability-ranks] to the identity of $\mathcal A$ with lower rank $\lambda$; it gives a regular $\rho\geq\lambda$. The same statement supplies arbitrarily large regular $\gamma$ sharply above $\rho$. Choose one uncountable, larger than the countable bisimplicial indexing category, and above the fixed bound in condition (ii) of [lem-coef-accessible-subdiagram-criterion] for $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\lambda)$. Then $\lambda\ll\gamma$: for $a<\gamma$ and $b<\lambda\leq\rho$, sharpness gives $a^b<\gamma$. These choices depend only on $f$ and the fixed universe, not the later arrow or subspace.

source.place: Definition A.2.6.3 and Proposition A.2.6.5, printed pp. 819–820; existence of sufficiently large sharp ranks.

proof.text: Now let $X\hookrightarrow Y$ and $C\subseteq Y$ satisfy the item hypotheses. By [lem-coef-simplicial-space-small-subobjects], $I=I_\gamma(Y)$ is a small $\gamma$-filtered poset, and the diagram $T(B)=(X\cap B\hookrightarrow B)$ has colimit $X\hookrightarrow Y$. Its terms are $\gamma$-presentable in the arrow category: both their endpoints have total size less than $\gamma$, so the arrow-presentability clause of that same lemma applies. Its colimit belongs to $\mathcal B$ because the given arrow is monomorphic and an $f$-local equivalence. Also $C\in I$.

source.place: Auxiliary bounded-presheaf presentation argument beneath the ancestor derived-adjunction paragraph.

proof.text: Use implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-coef-accessible-subdiagram-criterion] with $\sigma=\lambda$, $\tau=\gamma$, ambient category $\mathcal A$, subcategory $\mathcal B$, diagram $T:I\to\mathcal A$, and prescribed subset $S=\{C\}$. Steps 1–3 verify its closure, generation, local presentability, sharpness, size, presentability and colimit hypotheses. Since $\gamma$ is infinite, $|S|<\gamma$. Obtain $J\subseteq I$ containing $C$, of cardinality less than $\gamma$, $\lambda$-filtered in its inherited order, whose arrow colimit belongs to $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.5, printed p. 820, small filtered subdiagram approximation.

proof.text: Set $D=\bigcup_{B\in J}B$ in every bidegree. Each simplicial operator preserves every $B$, hence preserves their union, so $D$ is a simplicial subspace of $Y$. Regularity and $|J|,|B|<\gamma$ give $|D|<\gamma$, and $C\in J$ gives $C\subseteq D$. The restricted arrow diagram has colimit $X\cap D\hookrightarrow D$, directly by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: a compatible cocone defines its map on an element using any $B$ containing that element; two choices agree in a common upper bound in the nonempty directed poset $J$. The maps commute with operators because the cocone legs do. Apply this to both endpoints; the cocone squares give the square between the resulting maps, uniquely. On the source endpoint use the set identity $\bigcup_{B\in J}(X\cap B)=X\cap D$.

source.place: Elementary degreewise union and cocone computation for the chosen small directed family; written by the worker.

proof.text: By uniqueness of colimits the arrow of Step 5 is isomorphic to the colimit of Step 4. Repleteness of $\mathcal B$ puts $X\cap D\hookrightarrow D$ in $\mathcal B$, hence it is an $f$-local equivalence. Together with the containment and cardinal bound of Step 5, this proves the assertion for the single cardinal $\gamma$ fixed in Step 2.
